references.text: God declares that he will dwell among the children of Israel, and that they shall know him as their God who brought them out of Egypt.
God promises to set his dwelling place among the people and walk among them as their God.
God promises to dwell among the children of Israel when Solomon builds the temple, and that he will not forsake his people.
David urges the building of the sanctuary for the Lord God, so that the ark of the covenant and the holy vessels may be brought into the house.
God promises to establish his sanctuary among the people forever and dwell with them.
God declares that the temple is the place of his throne and the footstool of his feet, where he will dwell among the children of Israel forever.
The Lord promises to come and dwell among Zion, and many peoples shall join themselves to him.
The Word became flesh and took up residence (σκηνόω) among us - a fulfillment of God's promise to dwell among his people.
Stephen refers to the tabernacle of testimony that the fathers had in the wilderness, built according to the pattern Moses saw.
Believers are the temple of the living God, and God will dwell among them and walk among them.
The church grows into a holy temple in the Lord, a dwelling place for God in the Spirit.
Jesus is the servant of the sanctuary and the true tabernacle which the Lord has pitched, not man.
In the new Jerusalem, God's dwelling will be with humanity, and he shall dwell among them.
Ezekiel 37:27 fulfills and expands upon the promise in Exodus 25:8 of God's eternal dwelling among his people.
Ezekiel 43:9 shows the necessary cleansing that must occur before the promise of an eternal dwelling in Exodus 25:8 can be realized.
Exodus 29:45 confirms and specifies the purpose of the sanctuary mentioned in Exodus 25:8.
Ezekiel 37:26 transforms the temporary sanctuary of Exodus 25:8 into an eternal reality in the new covenant.
Leviticus 26:12 elaborates on the conditions for God's presence (as mentioned in Ex 25:8) to endure.
